Discovery Park Visitor Center.description: The Visitor Center is the usual orientation point for maps, restrooms, programs, and Loop Trail access, but renovation work may move or limit services through 2027.

North Beach and Hidden Valley Trail.description: North Beach is reached by a long forest-and-bluff descent, commonly via Hidden Valley Trail; the return climb, tides, mud, and limited facilities matter.

Fort Lawton historic district.description: The Fort Lawton district preserves military-era buildings, parade grounds, and cultural history near Daybreak Star; building interiors are not generally park space.

Evans Pool.description: Evans Pool is a staffed indoor aquatics facility beside the Community Center with separate admission, class schedules, lap-swim times, and maintenance closures.

Green Lake basketball and tennis courts.description: The east-side courts support basketball, tennis, and programmed recreation; reservations, leagues, and maintenance may limit casual use.

Woodland Park connection.description: The southwest connection links Green Lake to Woodland Park, sports fields, trails, and the zoo area across busy streets; use marked crossings.

Gas Works picnic shelter.description: The reservable picnic shelter provides covered gathering space near the main lawn; reservation, alcohol, grilling, and amplified-sound rules apply.

The Prow waterfront point.description: The Prow is the low waterfront point with close Lake Union views and skyline photos; the edge is unguarded and water entry remains prohibited.

North parking and comfort station.description: The north arrival concentrates the main parking, restrooms, and Burke-Gilman connection; the lot fills quickly during sunsets and major events.

Seward Park Audubon Center.description: The Audubon Center is a staffed environmental-education facility with its own programs, public hours, exhibits, and temporary closures.

Bailey Peninsula viewpoint.description: The peninsula's shoreline viewpoints look across Lake Washington toward Mount Rainier on clear days; weather, smoke, and tree cover affect visibility.

Seward Park tennis courts.description: The outdoor tennis courts sit in the developed recreation zone and may be occupied by lessons, leagues, or maintenance.

Upper picnic area and shelter.description: Upper picnic areas offer quieter gathering space above the shoreline loop; shelters and large events may require reservations and uphill access.

Foster Island.description: Foster Island extends the waterfront trail into wetlands and lake habitat on narrow paths and boardwalks that may flood or close during construction.

Rhododendron Glen.description: Rhododendron Glen is a wooded seasonal-bloom collection reached from central Arboretum paths, with slopes, damp ground, and peak spring color.

Arboretum Creek and Woodland Garden.description: The creek and woodland garden provide shaded, quieter paths near the visitor center; surfaces and drainage vary after rain.

Black Sun sculpture.description: Isamu Noguchi's Black Sun frames a distinctive Space Needle view near the museum and reservoir; it is public art, not climbing equipment.

Volunteer Park dahlia garden.description: The seasonal dahlia beds provide peak color in late summer and early fall; blooms and maintenance vary through the year.

Volunteer Park tennis courts.description: The public outdoor courts follow posted use and reservation rules, with leagues and maintenance sometimes limiting drop-in play.

Kerry Park east lawn.description: The small east lawn offers limited sitting space beside the main overlook; it becomes crowded at sunset and provides almost no weather protection.

Kerry Park west viewpoint.description: The west end opens toward Elliott Bay and the Olympic Mountains, offering a less central angle than the classic Space Needle composition.

Stairway to Bayview-Kinnear Park.description: The steep stair connection descends from the overlook toward the lower play area; it is not the step-free route and can be slippery in rain.

Queen Anne walking approach.description: Walking from Queen Anne Avenue avoids scarce curb parking but includes substantial neighborhood grades and uneven sidewalks in places.

Eagle sculpture.description: Alexander Calder's Eagle is the park's signature red sculpture and a useful meeting point on the central lawn near the main path.

Neukom Vivarium.description: Neukom Vivarium is a staffed indoor artwork built around a living nurse log, with access limited to posted pavilion hours.

Father and Son fountain.description: The Father and Son figures stand in a tidal fountain near the waterfront path; fountain operation varies and the basin is not a play area.

Pedestrian bridge over Elliott Avenue.description: The bridge carries the zigzag route over Elliott Avenue and rail infrastructure, connecting upper arrivals to the waterfront with sustained grades.

Seattle Aquarium Ocean Pavilion.description: The Ocean Pavilion is a separately ticketed aquarium facility integrated with Overlook Walk, with its own entrance, hours, security, and capacity limits.

Union Street pedestrian bridge.description: The Union Street bridge and elevator provide a practical accessible connection between downtown and the waterfront when lifts are operating.

Pier 66 and Bell Harbor promenade.description: The Bell Harbor promenade extends north past cruise and marina activity with skyline and bay views; ship operations can change pedestrian flow.

Golden Gardens beach volleyball courts.description: Sand volleyball courts sit in the lower beach zone and are heavily used in warm weather; organized play and events may take priority.

Golden Gardens duck pond and wetlands.description: The pond and wetland area provide bird habitat behind the beach; observe wildlife without feeding it and keep dogs out of protected areas.

North meadow picnic area.description: The north meadow offers open picnic and gathering space beyond the busiest bathhouse zone, with limited shade and seasonal event use.
